As the SOC of the BESS units drop further and reaches below the minimum SOC threshold of 15%(SOC ), L the PFMS brings online an appropriate number of generators to support the load (Algorithm 4). As shown in Figure 8 (b), the output of the BESS units drop around t ∼1120 second, the generator units come online at the same time and deliver an aggregate output power of 44 MW. Since the generator out- put is higher than the loads, excess power of about 10 MW is used for charging the BESS units. This is seen by the increase in SOC in Figure 8 (c). As seen in Figure 8 (d), the loads do not experience any impact as the energy source is changing (between the BESS and generators). Next, stable utility power returns, which is simulated by increasing the utility voltage back to 230 kV at t ∼1510 second, as seen in Figure 9(a). The PFMS initiates the grid reconnection process to reconnect the power system to the grid using an open transition (Algorithm 5) after the reconnection criteria is met around t ∼1565 second. As shown in Figure 9 (b), the loads are disconnected at t ∼1565 second, and the compute/IT workloads are supported by the UPS. The PFMS then reduces the aggregate generator power output to zero around t ∼1565 and the generators are turned off, as shown in Figure 9(b). Next, the PFMS puts the BESS units into idle mode, and their aggregate output is shown to drop to zero as well. At this point, there are no energy sources supplying power to the loads, and the compute/IT load are supported by the UPS. The PFMS then closes the utility breaker at t ∼1600 second, and the power supplied by the grid is shown to increase as it supports the total load in Figure 9(b). The interruptible workloads return, which is simulated by the multiplier M=1 around t =1620 second, and is confirmed by the total load increasing from 35 MW to approximately 45 MW in Figure 9(d). Overall, it took less than 30 seconds to reconnect the power system to the power grid after confirming the stable grid conditions.
